clinical_detail: Phase I study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03517176; ANZCTR ACTRN12618000804280) in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, conducted at three Australian centres between 13 August 2018 and 19 June 2020. CEND-1 given at 1.6 or 3.2 mg/kg as a slow intravenous push over 1 min, first as monotherapy at a run-in day, then in combination with nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine at cycle 1 day 1 and cycle 6 day 1. Plasma sampled pre-dose and at 3, 15, 30 min, 1 h, 3/4 h and 6/8 h after infusion.

agents.name: CEND-1 (iRGD) - preclinical peptide
agents.sequence: CRGDKGPDC (cyclic; S-S bonded through the cysteine side chains)
agents.sequence_source: METHODS 4: 'The cyclic iRGD/CEND-1 peptide [sequence: CRGDKGPDC] ... It has a cyclic structure (S-S bonded through the cysteine side chains).' Also INTRODUCTION: 'a nine-amino-acid cyclic tumour-penetrating peptide (amino acid sequence: CRGDKGPDC)'.
agents.chemical_identifier: sourced from GenScript (Piscataway, NJ, USA) or CPC Scientific (Hangzhou, China); purity >95%
agents.group_n: 3 male mice per dose level (each animal used for a single timepoint)
agents.group_n_quote: Because of volume limitations in the mice and rats, each animal was used for one time point sampling, limiting the statistical analysis of the data.
agents.dose: 1.5, 4.5 and 13.5 mg/kg (mice). Other species: 1, 5 and 50 mg/kg per Methods for rats/dogs/monkeys, although Table 1 lists 1, 5 and 75 mg/kg for rats and dogs and 5 and 50 mg/kg for monkeys.
agents.dose_route_quote: following the intravenous injection of CEND-1 at various doses (1, 5 and 50 mg/kg for rats, dogs and monkeys; 1.5, 4.5 and 13.5 mg/kg for mice)
agents.half_life: 0.306 h, 0.344 h and 0.547 h at 1.5, 4.5 and 13.5 mg/kg respectively (mouse, Table 1); text states 'approximately 20-25 min in mice'
agents.cmax: Table 1 reports C0 (back-extrapolated concentration at time zero), not an observed Cmax: 10,343 ng/mL (1.5 mg/kg), 40,291 ng/mL (4.5 mg/kg), 68,358 ng/mL (13.5 mg/kg). The Discussion equates the two: 'this dose results in a Cmax (C0) of approximately 40 microg/mL'.
agents.tmax: not reported for mice (Table 1 has no Tmax row for the animal species; dosing was an intravenous bolus/infusion)
agents.auc: AUC0-inf = 1476, 3695 and 10,569 h*ng/mL at 1.5, 4.5 and 13.5 mg/kg (mouse, Table 1)
agents.pk_quote: UNITS CHECK (Table 1): the column header is printed as 't1/2h'. This is a half-life in HOURS, not a rate constant in h-1. Confirmation from the body text: 'The average half-lives were approximately 20-25 min in mice, 30 min in rats and 40 min in dogs' - 0.306 h = 18 min and 0.344 h = 21 min, matching. The parameter name t1/2 and the body text were trusted over any ambiguity in the header string, and no ln(2)/k conversion was performed. Phase: the body says exposure 'increased with dose in a more-than-dose-proportional manner, with rapid elimination' but never formally names the phase for the animal half-lives, so 'unspecified' is used. Table 1 also gives V 449/599/1007 mL/kg and Cl_obs 1016/1205/1277 mL/hr/kg in mice. Other species (Table 1): rat t1/2 0.248-0.805 h, dog 0.615-0.668 h, monkey 0.888-0.956 h; 'In monkeys, the average half-life was approximately 55 min.'

agents.pk_quote: The PK was characterised by a rapid distribution phase and linear elimination phase with a half-life of approximately 2 h in humans - this Discussion sentence is the basis for the 'elimination' phase label. Results add: 'The median half-life values of CEND-1 (T1/2) were between 1.6 and 1.8 h over PK sampling timepoints. Mean clearance (CL) values were between 106.8 mL/h/kg and 266.5 mL/h/kg. The terminal volume of distribution (Vz) mean values were between 220.9 mL/kg and 277.4 mL/kg'. Peak concentrations occurred at the first post-dose sample: 'peak plasma concentration occurring at the first post-dose PK sampling timepoint (3 min post-dose)', consistent with the ~0.06-0.12 h Tmax values. Table 2 additionally lists lambda_last 0.3607/0.4082/0.4338 1/h - a rate constant which was recorded verbatim and NOT converted to a half-life.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figure 1A-C (human plasma); Figure 3 (mouse tissue concentrations over time)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Mean (±SD) plasma CEND-1 concentrations over time in pancreatic cancer patients by dose level (1.6 mg/kg or 3.2 mg/kg)
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 1 plots human plasma CEND-1 concentration versus time at run-in, cycle 1 day 1 and cycle 6 day 1. Figure 3 plots quantitative radioactivity (CEND-1 microg equivalents/g) in perfused mouse tissues at 0.5, 3 and 8 h after 5 mg/kg [3H]-CEND-1, i.e. a tissue concentration-time series rather than a plasma curve. No plasma concentration-time figure is presented for the mouse; mouse plasma data appear only as derived parameters in Table 1.

bioanalytical_method: Validated LC-MS/MS for plasma CEND-1 (AB Sciex Triple Quad API 5500, positive ESI, transition m/z 495.4 to 69.9; tolbutamide or leuprorelin acetate internal standards). Tissue disposition measured by quantitative whole-body autoradiography (QWBA) and quantitative radioactivity analysis (QRA) of [3H]-CEND-1. Non-compartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin v6.1.
bioanalytical_quote: Plasma CEND-1 was quantified by validated liquid chromatography coupled with a tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS) assay.
notes: UNITS TRAP RESOLVED: Table 1's parameter column is printed as 't1/2h'. It is a half-life expressed in hours, not a rate constant in h-1. Evidence used: the parameter name is t1/2, and the body text states 'The average half-lives were approximately 20-25 min in mice, 30 min in rats and 40 min in dogs' and 'In monkeys, the average half-life was approximately 55 min', which match the tabulated 0.306-0.547 h (mouse), 0.248-0.805 h (rat), 0.615-0.668 h (dog) and 0.888-0.956 h (monkey). No ln(2)/k conversion was performed by the curator. RATE CONSTANT HANDLED SEPARATELY: human Table 2 lists lambda_last of 0.3607, 0.4082 and 0.4338 1/h; these were recorded verbatim in pk_quote and were NOT converted into half-lives, because the same table already reports the fitted t1/2 values. Cmax vs C0: Table 1 reports C0 (concentration back-extrapolated to time zero) for the animal species, not an observed Cmax; the Results text nonetheless describes 'systemic exposure of CEND-1, expressed as Cmax and AUClast' and the Discussion says 'this dose results in a Cmax (C0) of approximately 40 microg/mL'. Both the label and the value are recorded so the distinction is not lost. No tmax is reported for any animal species (intravenous dosing); tmax IS reported for humans (0.063-0.117 h). No absorption half-life is reported for any species, as all dosing was intravenous. DOSE INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE BODY: Methods 4.1 states '1, 5 and 50 mg/kg for rats, dogs and monkeys', but Table 1 lists 1, 5 and 75 mg/kg for rats and dogs; both are recorded. Study-type scope: this article covers mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey and human; the mouse PK values (t1/2 0.306/0.344/0.547 h) are the ones matching the PEPLIFE2 header rows. Curation rule applied: procedural probe, contrast and anaesthetic substances are documented here rather than listed as agents - Evans blue (33.3 mg/kg i.v., extracted from tissue in N,N-dimethylformamide and quantified at 600 nm), Gd-DTPA, Gd-DOTA and gadoxetic acid (Gd-EOB-DTPA) MRI contrast agents, and ketamine (70 mg/kg) plus xylazine (10 mg/kg) and isoflurane as anaesthetics. nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine are co-administered background chemotherapy rather than true comparator arms; they are given role 'comparator' only because the schema role enum has no 'co-administered therapy' option. Excision and extraction of tissues for QRA and Evans blue quantification were treated as bioanalysis of in vivo samples, not as a separate ex vivo experiment, consistent with the handling of plasma assays.
